## 1. Complements of place

The exercise of lesson 75 was intended to remind you of this notion which we had sketched out in our first lessons. Today we are going to try to put our ideas definitively in order.

Latin distinguishes four sorts of places, which we are going to examine successively:

### A. The place where one is. Question: Ubi?

> Ubi es?, *where are you?* — Sum in horreo, *I am in the loft.*

As a general rule, the complement preceded by in, is in the *ablative*,

EXCEPT in a few particular cases: names of towns and of small islands, words domus, rus, and humus, with which the preposition in is not used:

1° IF THESE NOUNS HAVE A *locative* (proper singular nouns of the 1st and the 2nd declension), IT IS USED:

> Sum Massiliae, Lugduni, Sami, domi, ruri, humi: *I am in Marseille, in Lyon, in Samos (small island), at home, in the country, on the ground.*

2° IN THE OPPOSITE CASE, *ablative without* in:

> Sum Athenis, es Chicagine: *I am in Athens, you are in Chicago.*

Remarks. — IF ONE OF THESE NOUNS IS ACCOMPANIED BY A QUALIFYING OR POSSESSIVE ADJECTIVE OR PRECEDED BY AN APPOSITION, ONE FALLS BACK INTO THE NORMAL CASE:

> In nova domo, in dura humo, in urbe Massilia: *in a new house, on the hard earth, in the town of Marseille.*

(But exceptionally with the possessive adjective: domi tuae, *at your place*, instead of in domo tua, which is also sometimes used.)

— IF THE APPOSITION IS FOUND *after* THE NAME OF THE TOWN, THE LATTER IS *treated separately* ACCORDING TO THE GENERAL RULE:

> Massiliae, in urbe Marii: *in Marseille, in the town of Marius.*

### B. The place where one is going. Question: Quo?

> Quo vadis?, *Where are you going?* — Eo in Italiam, *I am going to Italy.*

As a general rule, the complement, preceded by in, is in the *accusative*,

EXCEPT for the nouns which were exceptions to the previous general rule, with which the *accusative without* in is used:

> Eo: Romam, domum, domum tuam, Athenas, Samum, but in urbem Romam, in veterem domum, finally Massiliam, in urbem Marii.

### C. The place one comes from. Question: Unde?

> Unde exis?, *Where are you coming out of?* — Exeo e schola polytechnica, *I am coming out of the polytechnic school.*

As a general rule, the complement, preceded by ex (e before a consonant) is in the *ablative*.

But ex disappears in front of the words of the previous categories, always with the same exceptions:

> Exeo: Massilia, domo, domo mea, etc… Massilia, ex urbe Marii.

As an exercise, you can take up all the examples of A. again to answer successively the questions B. and C. and take the opportunity to conjugate the verbs ire and exire. E.g.: eo in horreum, exeo ex horreo, is Massiliam, exis Massilia, etc.

### D. The place through which one passes. Question: Qua?

> Qua transivisti?, *Which way did you pass?* — Iter feci per urbem, *I passed through the town.*

General rule: per and the *accusative*.

Exception: THE WORDS iter, mare, terra, porta, pons, and via ARE NOT PRECEDED BY per AND ARE PUT IN THE *ablative*.

E.g.: Itinere longo, terra marique peregrinavit: *he travelled by a long itinerary, by land and by sea.* — Porta Capena, via Aurelia: *by the Capena gate, by the Aurelian Way.* — Ponte transiit: *he crossed by a bridge.*

## 2. Correlative adverbs of place

You will find a summary table of them in the grammatical appendix. What follows will be even more summary.

When the complement of place is not a noun, it can be an adverb. Thus, to the question ubi? correspond the adverbs:

- DEMONSTRATIVE: ibi, *there*; ibidem, *in the same place*; hic, *there where I am*; istic, *there where you are*; illic, *there where he is*; these last correspond respectively to the adjective pronouns hic, iste, ille;
- RELATIVE: ubi, *there where*; ubicumque, *everywhere where*;
- INDEFINITE: alibi, *elsewhere*; ubique, *everywhere*; ubivis, *no matter where*.

Other adverbs, constructed in a similar way, answer the three other questions. Examples:

- Quo? — eo, *(towards) there*; istuc, *(towards) there where you are* (vid. L. 75, N. 2); alio, *elsewhere (towards another place)*.
- Unde? — inde, *from there*; illinc, *from there where he is* (vid. L. 68, N. 4); aliunde, *from elsewhere*.
- Qua? — ea, *by there*; hac, *by there where I am*; alia, *by another place*. Note these long a's, as in the ablative singular of the 1st declension.

## 3. Prefixes

We have been able to see that Latin used numerous compound words, formed with the help of prefixes and suffixes. E.g.: with vocare, *to call*, one constructs provocare, *to call out, to provoke* (prefix pro-); but also vocitare, *to call frequently* (suffix -ita).

Let us examine today a few formations of words with the help of a few prefixes, which are at the same time PREPOSITIONS (not all of them are).

1° ab (+ abl., a before a consonant) indicates *moving away*:

- ferre\*, *to carry*; auferre\*, *to carry off* (perfect abstuli, supine ablatum);
- rapere, *to ravish*; abripere, *to tear away*.

2° ad (+ acc.) indicates *bringing together* or *addition*:

- afferre\*, *to bring* (pft. attuli, supine allatum; vid. sup. abstuli, ablatum);
- dare, *to give*; addere, *to add, to put in more* (addidi, additum).

3° cum (+ abl.) indicates the idea of *action in common*, of *union*, of *reinforcement*:

- colloqui, *to speak with, to converse*; collocare, *to place together*;
- conficere (from facere), *to do completely*;
- conferre\* (from ferre\*), *to gather, to compare* (cf. L. 76, N. 4).

We leave it to you, if you feel like it, to look for other verbs formed with these three prefixes.

N.B. — Note that, for reasons of euphony (the opposite of «cacophony»), the prefix and even the word that follows it sometimes undergo notable alterations.

## 4. The gender of nouns (continued)

What do you think of: mors, artifex, solitudo, latus, scriba, exemplar, volucris?

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

mortis, f., *death*; artificis, m., *artist, artisan*; solitudinis, f., *desert*; lateris, n., *side*; scribae, m., *office employee*; exemplaris, n. (gen. pl. -ium), *model*; volucris, feminine of the adjective volucer, -cris, -cre.

</details>
